Could you tell us where these villages are, Gramocelj, Prilep, Shaptej, and Glodjane, from where fire was opened on MUP and VJ members from infantry weapons, rocket-launchers, machine-guns, mortars, and recoilless guns?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I'd remind you that on the 8th of August, 1998 -- I'll retract that statement. What would you like me to say, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I can see here that KLA activities are mentioned in the villages of Gramocelj, Prilep, Shaptej, and Glodjane, that fire was opened at MUP and VJ members from infantry weapons, rocket-launchers, machine-guns, mortars, and recoilless guns.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, we are talking about the same areas that we have discussed discussed in considerable detail and which I've recognised were under fire for a lot of the time in 1998/1999. And these villages of Glodjane, Prilep, Riznik keep reappearing, which indicates the intensity of the operations in this area, you know, relatively close to the boarder of Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: There is this abbreviation BST, that stands for recoilless guns, which goes to show that the KLA were using such guns.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that was in the report, sir, then I would accept it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us take a look at item 3. Am I right when I say, sir, that in this item it is stated that army units support MUP units in accordance with the decision on engagement?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is what appears in this report, I'm sure it is true. I just draw the Court's attention to the amount of ammunition fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we please show item 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Under 3: "The commander of the 3rd Army decided to support MUP units in routing the DTS in the area of the villages of Gramocelj, Prilep, and Glodjane, with the aim of pushing the DTS away from the Djakovica-Decani-Pec main road"?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, that's in total agreement what I've been saying throughout this discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see document D005-0691. Just a moment. Ms. O'Leary will immediately say if I got the number right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: These, sir, are the minutes of a meeting between army command organs at the forward command post and the commanders of subordinated units which was held on the 17th of August. And about Junik, please take a look at paragraph 6. The sixth paragraph: "The army commander stated that Junik had not been destroyed, that there were no civilian casualties, and that there were no mass graves of which the world had been accusing us. These were facts which the VJ stood by while everything else is either propaganda or politics that must be opposed by all other members of society and the state organs."

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I think I've been trying to explain to the Court that one was attempting to report accurately as possible and that some of the claims that the media and other people were making in the worldwide press were not correct, so I stand by what I've said. My reports at the time were accurate and correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now -- but do you agree that at that time the commander of the 3rd Army was General Samardzic?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Forgive me. Which date are we now talking about, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The 17th of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect, sir, if this general has signed this paper, then he was presumably the person who wrote it, so I would accept that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In principle do you know who was commander of the 3rd Army from about mid-1998 until the end of that year?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially I think it was General Pavkovic who had been the corps commander in Pristina. When exactly he changed over to 3rd Army commander, I'm not -- I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us see document D004-2953, please. I apologise again, actually it's Exhibit D333.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Colonel, this is an order issued by the General Staff on the 17th of August, 1998. What you see in the first paragraph is the following: "It is stated that in the period from the 13th to the 15th of August, a team of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army carried out a tour of inspection of part of the commands and units." An order is issued with regard to that so let us go to page 2 and take a look at item 4. Is it correct that the Chief of General Staff, under 4, orders that part of the sabotage and terrorist forces from -- should be prevented from spilling over to KiM territory in the area of the Raska Polim district and the Jablanica and Juzma Morava district. Coordination is to be continued and joint action with the MUP forces and in keeping with the assessments, support -- the MUP forces should be supported in destroying the DTG, but without disturbing the carrying out of the main tasks of the VJ units."

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, if those are the orders given by the Vojska Yugoslavia, then I presume they are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Let us see the last page of this document, please, where you will see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see that this is signed by the Chief of General Staff, General Momcilo Perisic?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. But I think this was, if I remember rightly, possibly General Perisic's last visit down to the operation area, but I can't be certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I don't know that, but we'll see about that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see document D004-2965, please. I am again being corrected, it's Exhibit D334.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Colonel, we have before us an order by the commander of the 3rd Army. In the introductory part it says: "Pursuant to GS VJ orders, strictly confidential number 02/10-91 of 17 August 1998, with the aim of taking measures to raise the level of combat readiness of all command and units engaged in the area of KiM to a level that would ensure the successful completion of tasks, I here by order:" Please take a look at item 4(a)on page 4. Items 4(a) and 4(b).

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm referring to page 4 of the English version, and in B/C/S the page number is 2, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Colonel, at the level of the 3rd Army, is this order an implementation of the order of the General Staff, dated 17 August 1998, which we saw a short while ago?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be the normal process of orders down the chain of command, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see document D179.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Colonel, this is a directive of the General Staff of the VJ of the 16th of January 1999. The heading reads "Directive to engage the VJ to prevent forced introduction of a multinational NATO brigade in KiM." I wanted to go through all these documents to cover the period -- let me ask you what was the political and security situation in mid-January 1999? Can you enlighten us? I'm of course referring to Kosovo and Metohija and Yugoslavia too.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: In January 1999 the Court would be aware that a Kosovo Verification Mission had been in place headed by Ambassador Walker with General Drewienkiewicz, DZ for short. I think that had been in position since October 1998, or thereabouts. As we heard yesterday, there was ongoing incidents in the area of Podujevo, and then in the new year there was the serious incident at Racak. It was quite clear then that probably a political solution was not going to be -- was not going to succeed. And therefore both sides, I would suggest, were considering the very serious position that we were now facing in Kosova-Metohija, and that, as we all know, developed into NATO bombing in March.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But in the introduction we see the mention of a forced introduction of a multinational brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now go to page 2 and item 1.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And I will read out to you the relevant paragraph. "The introduction of a multinational brigade would be preceded by an ACTORDER by the NATO command." I would be interested in your comment about this ACTORDER. When was it first implemented, and how did things develop?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, with great respect, an ACTORDER is issued by the Supreme Allied Commander Europe, a four star general, in this case General Wes Clark. I think for a mere colonel to offer comment on his orders is not appropriate. I believe the ACTORDER -- the ACTORD, was asked for by General Clark I think in October or November 1998. And this was a process of escalating the pressure on the FRY to come to some arrangement by way that the situation could be salvaged before action took place on both sides of the border. I was in Kosovo when this order was given and part of the order was that the Vojska Yugoslavia would withdraw back to its bases, which again is detailed in one of my reports, and the Vojska Yugoslavia did withdraw back. And one of the problems that I had mentioned to my superiors was that if the Serbian security forces withdrew from certain areas, then this space could be, maybe, would be filled by the KLA. And that again is detailed in one of my reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. I don't want to interrupt you, I will continue from where we broke off.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is a convenient time. We will have the second break. We resume at 1.00 for what will be a nearly three quarter of an hour session. 1.00 we resume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, you have some matter to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Let the witness come in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we have to do is to -- we need to have the Prosecution reiterate its agreement to the admission of the Defence exhibits used by the Defence. The Prosecution has in fact agreed, but we also have to seek your leave for its admission into the case file. This was the instruction I was given, that I was to seek it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You would like to have one or a number of exhibits admitted, Mr. Djurdjic? A number?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, according to the list that the OTP agreed to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, if it's by agreement, we will most certainly receive what you propose.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you going to move for them individually, or do you move for them all to be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Frankly speaking, I do not understand, but I believe that individually is the way we want to proceed, for an individual number to be assigned to each document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received. There are five of them, I believe; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are four, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I have a list of five. Which on that list is the one which you are not tendering?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is D004-2681. That is in fact a book which is on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. The other four will be received. I will pass the list to the Court Officer, and the last one on that list will not be received. She will now announce the numbers for them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, exhibit numbers will be assigned as follows: 65 ter 4012 will become Exhibit D388; 65 ter 2136 will become Exhibit D389; Defence document D005-0688 will become Exhibit D390; And the last document, D005-0693 will become Exhibit D391. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Colonel, but let us latch on to where we broke off before. So this directive was adopted at a time when there was an impending danger for the FRY of the activation of the ACTORD. Would you now please look at Roman numeral II, page 2, the use of the VJ, last sentence. "In coordination with the forces of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, a block of Siptar forces in broader regions and at axis of introduction, and prevent them from acting in concert with NATO forces." That is the first stage. Am I right when I say that this directive anticipates -- foresees the coordinated action of the forces of the MUP and of the VJ forces in the event of the activation of the order?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems a perfectly reasonable assumption to be made by the forces of Yugoslavia. If they understood that they were facing a possible attack from NATO.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I now turn to 3; namely item 3.1. The tasks of the 3rd Army, that is on page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Does it say by your request the following units shall be subordinate to you, BG-252/252, armoured brigade from the 1st Army, the BG-37/37th Motorised Brigade from 2nd Army, and BG 3 Tactical Group Vihor from the KSJ special unit corps?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it says, sir, and these are some of the units that I think I reported on being present during the last days of my time down in Kosovo. So those are correct, as reported in my reports, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at Defence Exhibit D343.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Colonel, this is an order by the commander of the 3rd Army of the 27th of January, 1999: "For the use of the 3rd Army in preventing the forceful introduction of a NATO brigade, it's routing, and the destruction of Siptar terrorist forces in Kosova-Metohija?" Would it be fair to say that this was in fact the implementation of measures stemming from the directive of the 16th of January, 1999, which was brought by the Chief of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: This appears to be following the normal military chain of command, so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And under item 4, number 4, that is also on page 4, it is also ordered that in the event this order is put into practice in concert with MUP forces, DTS should be countered and prevented from linking to or cooperating with the NATO Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again this seems quite standard procedure, and linking with the MUP would be totally proper and correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. Now, I should like us to go back to October 1998. What do you know about the Holbrooke-Milosevic Agreement?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the Court, I don't see how I can possibly answer that question. I mean, I knew that Ambassador Holbrooke was in talks with President Milosevic, but what they said together, I was not present at, so I can't offer any help on that particular question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But do you know whether any agreement was reached between Holbrooke and Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, sir, the Ambassador Holbrooke was there, if I remember correctly, right up until March the 22nd, 23rd, when it was quite clear that the negotiations had failed, and that's really my only comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We shall move on. Do you know anything about the agreement on the Kosovo Verification Mission and the subsequent October Agreements that were reached in 1998 between the FRY on the one part, and NATO on the other, and the OSCE, naturally?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, to make things short, if you did participate in that and if you have any information, please tell me so; if not, tell me so also so that we do not lose any time over any information that might have been imparted from a third source or second-hand information?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I will not be rushed in my answers. You are asking detailed questions; I'm attempting to give you the correct answers. I was part of the -- I briefed the Verification Mission in Belgrade. I placed them in position in Kosovo. But as to other detailed planning that took place between the Verification Mission, OSCE, I was far too busy doing other things in Kosovo. I was obviously aware of these negotiations, and I was informed as appropriate. But it was important that the KVM, the Kosovo Verification Mission, and the OSCE remained apart from the original parties that had been engaged in Kosova-Metohija, mainly ourselves as the defence attaches and the Vojska Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, it was never my intention to rush you. I just wanted us to clarify to see whether we can indeed discuss that topic or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see Exhibit P836.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is an agreement between KDOM and the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia which was signed on the 25th of October, 1999, between Messrs. Djordjevic and Byrnes. Were you acquainted with the content of this agreement?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I was aware, sir. I know Mr. Byrnes because we worked quite closely. But as to this -- as to this document, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I should like to now ask you to assist us in one matter and to explain something to us. Please take a look at item 3, this sentence: "The police will use the Orahovac-Suva Reka-Dulje-Malisevo road. And in the coming 15 days, it will not move along the Malisevo-Orahovac road. The Malisevo-Orahovac road must remain fully open at all times for unimpeded and free traffic of flow of people and goods." You are familiar with the terrain in question, and therefore I should like to ask you this: From Malisevo to Orahovac, as the crow flies, what is the distance, the direct distance along that road in kilometres?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's between 12 and 15 kilometres, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we had a better map, I should like you to draw it for us on the map, but as it is not very good copy, let us at least have it in oral statement. So during those 15 days, the road would be available for the traffic of policemen from Orahovac to Suva Reka and then to Dulje and Malisevo. I believe that from your experience, according to what you have stated in your statements, you yourself moved along that road. How many kilometres was that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: From where to where, sir? From Orahovac to Malisevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: From Orahovac to Suva Reka, that is what is written here, Orahovac Suva Reka, and then on to Dulje?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you go on the direct route from Orahovac on the cross-country route, it's probably 10 to 15 a kilometres to Suva Reka, and then a further 8, 9 kilometres to Blace. If you go from Orahovac south down to Zrte [phoen] and then to Prizren and up, I would think it's approximately 40 or 50 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you also factor in the road from Dulje to Malisevo in that distance? You said Orahovac to Suva Reka and then Suva Reka to Dulje, and then Dulje-Malisevo.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dulje-Malisevo is approximately 16 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So it would be approximately around 60 kilometres, this circuitous road, to be precise?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, approximately so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now take a look at P837, please. It should be there. It should be in your domain.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is page number 1 which is not of the essence because the substance of the document is on the second and third pages of this document, and that is what the question refers to. Do you remember or did you perhaps participate in the visit of General Clark and General Naumann in Belgrade -- to Belgrade in October, one of the results of which was this agreement of the 25th of October, 1998, which deals with army units which remain outside barracks. As far as I know you participated in those meetings?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I helped the American embassy with various meetings, but I don't recall specifically attending this meeting because it's an extremely high-powered meeting with General Naumann and General Wesley Clark there as well. So, I'm sorry, I don't think I can help you on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at item 5. I didn't mean that you participated in the making of this agreement in it's -- but that you participated later in its realisation, in its adoption, and that you are familiar with this particular item 5. It is stated here, Colonel, that except for VJ units currently re-enforcing border guard units, all other elements of the VJ remain Kosovo will return to garrisons except for three company-strength teams which will remain deployed there. Each will be tasked with protecting lines of communication between, A, Pec, Lapusnik, Pristina; B, Djakovica, Klina; and under C, Prizren, Suva Reka, Pristina. These three company-strong groups will return to garrison not later than one week after the signature of the political agreement."

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told the Court that I monitored these three company battle groups moving back to their barracks as detailed, and I think at that particular time I passed the information direct to General Clark's office, so I saw that they, as I've stated already, that the Vojska Yugoslavia had complied with the order that they would withdraw back to their barracks as detailed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Colonel, do you agree with me when I say that the FRY honoured the October Agreement and that the ACTORDER was never activated?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The initial ACTORD was never activated, no, because the FRY [realtime transcript read in error "never"] complied with what was required.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. And then you assisted in the introduction of the Kosovo Verification Mission, that's what you said. I would now like to go through some reports of the Kosovo Verification Mission to see whether you have any knowledge about some interesting events, and therefore I would like to call Exhibit D157.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you move on, Mr. Djurdjic, page 59, line 24, the answer of the witness is said to conclude because the FRY never complied with what was required. I thought his answer was the opposite, that they did comply?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just so that that is noted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Colonel --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This doesn't seem to match. I said D157. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The first paragraph under the heading KLA, General Jankovic, it says: "The most significant activity by the KLA was in the General Jankovic line. Prior to the fighting this week, this region had been quiet; only the strategic [indiscernible]. The KLA activity has been limited to a small and insignificant inactive militia. Although support could always be found from across the border in Tetovo, It would appear that over 100 KLA crossed the border and encouraged the locals to leave. The incentive to move into the region is unclear, although a number of possibilities exist. By encouraging" -- Now, the following item reads: "By encouraging the movement of internally displaced persons, IDPs, the international media was able to claim a Serb offensive was underway." Colonel, we are speaking about the end of February and the beginning of March. Are you familiar with the activities of the KLA in the territory of the Kacanik municipality, I believe? And the villages are Kotlina, Livelja [phoen], and that area.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, sir, there was an attack in that area at this particular time and one or two MUP were killed, and hence the comments in this Kosovo verification paper, which as it says is a draft paper laying out what they think the situation is at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please go to page 2 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It says here: "The KLA forces in the Podujevo area were able to carry out an attack in the town itself - effectively beating the Serbs." Were you familiar with that, and were you in Kosovo and Metohija at that period?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, sir, there is a report of mine, I believe, on this particular instant that the -- one of the KLA headquarters by Mitrovica, by Gora and Bradas, a village closer to Podujevo, and the KLA had carried out an assault because this -- this main route going north from Pristina through Podujevo to Kursumlje and on to Nis was the main supply route for the Vojska Yugoslavia and all forces in there, and therefore not unnaturally, the VJ and the MUP required to keep this route open, and therefore a threat by the KLA to their main logistic supply route was critical to their operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But here the victory of the KLA in the town of Podujevo is alleged.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, as I've said many times, the one force would gain the upper-hand and then some days later the other force would retake it. So if the KLA called it a victory, that is entirely up to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Unfortunately we broke off because it was time for a break, and you were speaking about your apprehension that after the October Agreement, once the military withdraws, the vacated areas would be taken by the KLA which eventually happened. Did I understand you to say that, sir? Or is it, did I actually correctly understand you to say that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir. And I've given that in evidence to the Court, and I believe it's in several of my reports, again attempting to make my seniors understand the difficulties of this particular scenario, situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see D002-4026. It's a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me first ask you, Colonel, to tell me which territories those are that were taken by the KLA when the VJ and other security forces withdrew and all that after the signing of the October Agreements in 1998?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking a totally unanswerable question. My reports at the time specified the changes of occupation, and this happened throughout Kosovo. You are quite right in saying that the KLA attacked Podujevo. They were then driven out of Podujevo. When the VJ combat groups withdrew under the NATO ACTORDER, the KLA followed up, and several MUP were killed, I think, on the main Pristina-Pec road in the area of, I think, Lapusnik Kumeranje [phoen]. So wherever there was a movement of Serbian security forces out of an area, the KLA would come back in. I mean, this happened all over Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, but we have information that the military withdrew to the barracks apart from those three companies under the agreement, and that the police continued to engage in their activities in accordance with the agreement. Mr. Zurapi who was Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command of the KLA said that the KLA had occupied a greater territory than it had held before the summer offensive in 1998.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure on how to answer that question. I've indicated that during 1998, and I have stated in reports that approximately 70 per cent of the area was under KLA command, and that flowed backwards and forwards. If this gentleman has stated that, then I can't raise any comment on that, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now return to Exhibit D157 and go to the end of page -- or to the bottom of page 4 of the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Summary of events prior to 28 February 1999: "KLA appeared to have moved into the region in force and combined with a militia to a total force of 120 to 160. Locals heard some shooting from the village of Stremce, EM 1968." These must be the coordinates. "This village is virtually cut off during to a heavy fall of snow, and therefore any suspected activities cannot be confirmed by the locals, making them susceptible to rumour. The KLA told the villagers in the region to move out, nearly all of whom obliged by the 27th of February, leading to an IDP report on the 28th of February, 1999." Colonel, did you know at the time that the KLA was misusing civilians?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an OSCE KVM report. At that particular time I think I was probably one of the very few defence attaches still down in Kosovo, so if I was not in that area, then I can't confirm or deny this particular report, so I'm sorry, but you will have to ask people concerned with the KVM OSCE.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Colonel, these reports are just a tool for me to ask you whether you -- about your knowledge. Did you know at the time that the KLA was misusing civilians to their ends to create an apparent humanitarian disaster?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think with respect, sir, there was a human disaster, and there had been for several weeks. There had been many reports of internally displaced persons, as I indicated already in the Pagarusa valley, and one had seen villages on the move carrying all their worldly wealth in carts. I think what I've said answers the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Colonel, the question is simple, it follows from these reports that the KLA drove out people from their settlements and thus creating an apparent humanitarian disaster, invited journalists who kept reporting about that. Did you have knowledge of that at the time or not? I don't think that's a difficult question to answer.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you are inviting me to say is that the KLA was responsible for the internally displaced personnel. They may well have contributed to it. It was not a one-sided effort. The actions of the Serbian security forces had also contributed to it. The media was now growing in strength in Kosova-Metohija, and therefore, whoever could get the headlines got the credit. And it's simply a question of public relations on both sides, which, as we know, is very powerful with the media able to flash this -- these incidents around the world in a matter of seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us just go through one more document. I believe there's enough time left. Do you know, sir, that toward the end of 1998 and in 1999, the objective of the NATO member states was to be present in Kosovo as a military Verification Mission?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, if I understand your question, the Kosovo Verification Mission was suggested to be used as a tool in order to give all parties time to have a breathing space and to attempt to come to some peaceful solution in this area. And, therefore, the Kosovo Verification Mission, I believe, was accepted by the FRY authorities and headed, as I've said, by Ambassador Walker and General DZ, and they carried on their duties until early 1999 when they had to withdraw, on March 19th, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have mentioned a number of soldiers who were involved in the verification and who were members of the KVM as a civilian mission. And I have here a statement by Mr. Vollebaek which says that in March of -- in March 1999, Mr. Milosevic was opposed to the presence of NATO forces in Kosovo for the purpose of the completion of the verification.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would kindly ask my learned colleague if he could indicate the source of this statement that he is reading out, and if it could be displayed to the witness so he can review it before he is answering that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I am afraid we've run out of time for both of those things to occur. That will have to be taken up tomorrow. If you can get that documentation organised to assist the witness tomorrow. We must now adjourn to resume tomorrow at 2.15 p.m.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect, I'm sorry to interrupt. I had heard, or I was informed that I would be released today. If I'm to be kept tomorrow, sir, and it's 2.00, then I'm going to have logistic and business problems back in the United Kingdom. I appreciate this is minor request with Mr. Karadzic and other people around, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I am sorry, it's not a minor request, and I don't know the source of your information that you would be finished today. The cross-examination is continuing. It needs to finish. My present expectation is that it will finish tomorrow and re-examination, so that you can expect to be free after tomorrow. But we cannot do anything about that. We are programmed to sit either morning or afternoon, and we have been programmed tomorrow to sit in the afternoon at 2.15 so we can't -- there are no spare courtrooms, so we can't sit in the morning. I'm sorry about that. I hope you will be able to re-organisation in some way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We adjourn now until tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 28th day of October, 2009, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
